title: Client Level Segregation of Advisory and Distribution Activities
summary: Ensure client level segregation at IA’s group/family level, where existing clients cannot avail both advisory and distribution services within the same group/family.
trigger: IA's group/family of clients
required_action: Adopt a compliance and monitoring process to ensure client level segregation.
evidence: Documentation of the adopted compliance and monitoring process, annual certificate from auditor/statutory auditor.
verbatim_text: Existing clients, who wish to take advisory services, will not be eligible for availing distribution services within the group/family of IA. Similarly, existing clients who wish to take distribution services will not be eligible for availing advisory services within the group/family of IA.

title: Client Level Segregation of Advisory and Distribution Activities - New Clients
summary: New clients can avail either advisory or distribution services, but not both within the same group/family.
trigger: IA's group/family of clients
required_action: Make available to new clients the option to choose between advisory or distribution services at on-boarding.
evidence: Documentation of the on-boarding process and options provided to new clients.
verbatim_text: A new client will be eligible to avail either advisory or distribution services within the group/family of IA. However, the option to avail either advisory services or distribution services shall be made available to such client at the time of on boarding.

title: Client Level Segregation of Advisory and Distribution Activities - Client Definition
summary: Define clients as individual or non-individual, with discretion to continue holding assets under existing advisory/distribution arrangement.
trigger: IA's group/family of clients
required_action: Ensure that the client definition is clear and adhered to in practice.
evidence: Client records and documentation showing adherence to defined client types.
verbatim_text: Client under these guidelines shall include individual client or non-individual client.

title: Client Level Segregation of Advisory and Distribution Activities - Client Holding Assets
summary: Clients can continue holding assets under existing advisory/distribution arrangement, but not forced to liquidate/switch holdings.
trigger: IA's group/family of clients
required_action: Ensure that clients are not forced to liquidate or switch their existing holdings.
evidence: Client records and documentation showing adherence to the policy on holding assets.
verbatim_text: The client shall have discretion to continue holding assets prior to the applicability of this segregation under the existing advisory/distribution arrangement. However, the client shall not be forced to liquidate/switch such existing holdings.

title: Client Level Segregation of Advisory and Distribution Activities - PAN as Control Record
summary: Use Permanent Account Number (PAN) as the control record for client identification and segregation.
trigger: IA's group/family of clients
required_action: Maintain records using PAN as the control record.
evidence: Client records showing use of PAN as the control record.
verbatim_text: The Permanent Account Number (PAN) of each client shall be the control record for identification and client level segregation.

title: Client Level Segregation of Advisory and Distribution Activities - Family of Individual Clients
summary: For individual clients, family members are considered a single client with joint PAN.
trigger: IA's group/family of clients
required_action: Reckon dependent family members as a single client for the purpose of segregation.
evidence: Client records showing the treatment of family members under this policy.
verbatim_text: In case of an individual client, “family of client” shall be reckoned as a single client and PAN of all members in “family of client” would jointly and severally be the control record. However, the same is not applicable for non-individual clients.

title: Client Level Segregation of Advisory and Distribution Activities - Dependent Family Members Declaration
summary: Provide annual declaration or periodic update regarding dependent family members.
trigger: IA's group/family of clients
required_action: Obtain an annual declaration or periodic update from the client regarding dependent family members.
evidence: Client records showing declarations or updates provided by the client.
verbatim_text: The dependent family members shall be those members whose assets on which investment advisory is sought/provided, originate from income of a single entity i.e. earning individual client in the family. The client shall provide an annual declaration or periodic updation as the case maybe in respect of such dependent family members.

title: Client Level Segregation of Advisory and Distribution Activities - Direct Plans Recommendation
summary: Advise direct plans (non-commission based) of products only.
trigger: IA's group/family of clients
required_action: Recommend direct plans (non-commission based) to clients.
evidence: Client records and documentation showing the recommendation of direct plans.
verbatim_text: The IAs shall maintain on record an annual certificate from an auditor (in case of individual IA) and its statutory auditor (in case of a non-individual IA)

title: Annual Auditor Certificate for Client Segregation Compliance
summary: IA must obtain an annual certificate from an auditor confirming compliance with client level segregation requirements.
trigger: At the end of each financial year
required_action: Obtain and maintain on record an annual certificate from an auditor or statutory auditor.
evidence: Annual certificate from an auditor (individual IA) or its statutory auditor (non-individual IA).
verbatim_text: "(i) The IAs shall maintain on record an annual certificate from an auditor (in case of individual IA) and its statutory auditor (in case of a non-individual IA) confirming compliance with the client level segregation requirements as specified in Regulation 22 of the IA Regulations. Such annual certificate shall be obtained within 6 months of the end of the financial year and form part of compliance audit, in terms of Regulation 19(3) of the IA Regulations."

title: Investment Advisory Agreement with Clients
summary: IA must enter into an investment advisory agreement with clients that includes specific terms and conditions.
trigger: Before providing any investment advice or charging fees from a client
required_action: Enter into an investment advisory agreement with each client, ensuring it covers the mandatory terms provided in Annexure A. Additional terms can be included without diluting the IA Regulations.
evidence: Signed copy of the investment advisory agreement.
verbatim_text: "(ii) (a) Regulation 19(1)(d) of the IA Regulations provides that IA shall enter into an investment advisory agreement with its clients. The said agreement shall mandatorily cover the terms and conditions provided in Annexure A. (b) IA can include additional terms and conditions in the agreement without diluting the provisions of the IA Regulations and amendments thereto as well as circulars issued thereunder. (c) IA shall ensure that neither any investment advice is rendered nor any fee is charged until the client has signed the aforesaid agreement and provided copy of signed agreement to the client."

title: Fees Collection Methodology for Investment Advisory Services
summary: IA must charge fees from clients in either AUA mode or fixed fee mode, with specific limits.
trigger: When providing investment advisory services to a client
required_action: Charge fees according to the specified modes and limits: AUA mode (2.5% of AUA per annum) or fixed fee mode (INR 1,25,000 per annum).
evidence: Records of fees charged and supporting documents.
verbatim_text:
"(A) Assets under Advice (AUA) mode
(a) The maximum fees that may be charged under this mode shall not exceed 2.5 percent of AUA per annum per client across all services offered by IA.
(b) IA shall be required to demonstrate AUA with supporting documents like demat statements, unit statements etc. of the client.
(c) Any portion of AUA held by the client under any pre-existing distribution arrangement with any entity shall be deducted from AUA for the purpose of charging fee by the IA.
(B) Fixed fee mode
The maximum fees that may be charged under this mode shall not exceed INR 1,25,000 per annum per client across all services offered by IA."

title: Fees Collection Frequency and Change of Mode
summary: IA must charge fees annually under one mode and can only change the mode after 12 months.
trigger: When providing investment advisory services to a client
required_action: Charge fees on an annual basis, either in AUA or fixed fee mode. Change of mode is allowed only after 12 months from the last change.
evidence: Records of fees charged and signed agreement with clients.
verbatim_text: "(c) In case “family of client” is reckoned as a single client, the fee as referred above shall be charged per “family of client”. (b) IA shall charge fees from a client under any one mode i.e. (A) or (B) on an annual basis. The change of mode shall be effected only after 12 months of on boarding/last change of mode."

title: Fees Collection for Premature Termination
summary: IA must refund fees for unexpired period in case of premature termination, with a maximum breakage fee.
trigger: In the event of pre-mature termination of IA services
required_action: Refund the client the fees for the unexpired period and retain a maximum breakage fee not exceeding one quarter fee.
evidence: Records of fees charged, signed agreement with clients, and refund documentation.
verbatim_text:
"(c) If agreed by the client, IA may charge fees in advance. However, such advance shall not exceed fees for 2 quarters.
In the event of pre-mature termination of the IA services in terms of agreement, the client shall be refunded the fees for unexpired period. However, IA may retain a maximum breakage fee of not greater than one quarter fee."

title: Comply with Enhanced Qualification and Experience Requirements
summary: IA must comply with the applicable enhanced qualification and experience requirement within a period of three years, extended to September 30, 2025.
trigger: Registration as an individual IA or principal officer of a non-individual investment adviser
required_action: Obtain the required qualification and experience within the specified period
evidence: Certification from recognized bodies, relevant work experience documentation
verbatim_text: Regulation 7(1) of IA Regulations, was amended vide SEBI (Investment Advisers) (Amendment) Regulations, 2020 to specify enhanced qualification and experience requirement for individual investment adviser or a principal officer of a non-individual investment adviser and persons associated with investment advice. First proviso to the amended Regulation 7(1) specified that the individual investment advisers registered under these regulations or principal officer of a non-individual investment adviser registered under these regulations and persons associated with investment advice shall comply with the applicable enhanced qualification and experience requirement within a period of three years. The three-year period referred herein ended on September 30, 2023. Based on the representations received from various stakeholders and in view of the emerging landscape of the domain of investment advice, the first proviso to regulation 7(1) of SEBI (Investment Advisers) Regulations, 2013 has been further amended with effect from September 30, 2023, vide the SEBI (Investment Advisers) (Amendment) Regulations, 2023 dated October 09, 2023. Accordingly, the timeline to comply with the enhanced qualification and experience requirements under regulation 7(1) has been extended to September 30, 2025.

trigger: Upon application for prior approval and pending change in control
required_action: Inform all existing investors/clients of the proposed change before implementation.
evidence: Declaration cum undertaking signed by authorized signatories.
verbatim_text: ii. pursuant to grant of prior approval by SEBI, the incumbent shall inform all the existing investors/ clients about the proposed change prior to effecting the same, in order to enable them to take informed decision regarding their continuance or otherwise with the new management;

title: Comply with ‘fit and proper person’ criteria
summary: Investment Advisers must ensure that all individuals involved meet the specified fit and proper person criteria.
trigger: Upon application for prior approval
required_action: Ensure compliance with the ‘fit and proper person’ criteria as specified in Schedule II of Securities and Exchange Board of India (Intermediaries) Regulations, 2008.
evidence: Declaration cum undertaking signed by authorized signatories.
verbatim_text: iii. the ‘fit and proper person’ criteria as specified in Schedule II of Securities and Exchange Board of India (Intermediaries) Regulations, 2008 are complied with.

title: Obtain approval/NOC from stock exchanges/clearing corporations/depositories
summary: Investment Advisers must obtain necessary approvals or NOCs from relevant stock exchanges, clearing corporations, and depositories.
trigger: Upon application for prior approval if incumbent is a registered member of such entities
required_action: Obtain written approval/NOC from all relevant stock exchanges/clearing corporations/depositories where the incumbent is a member/depository participant.
evidence: Self-attested copies of approvals/NOCs.
verbatim_text: h. In case the incumbent is a registered stock broker, clearing member, depository participant, in addition to the above, it shall obtain approval /NOC from all the stock exchanges/clearing corporations/depositories, where the incumbent is a member/depository participant and submit self-attested copy of the same to SEBI.

title: Ensure validity period for prior approval
summary: Investment Advisers must ensure that their prior approval is valid within a specified timeframe.
trigger: Upon obtaining prior approval from SEBI
required_action: File application for fresh registration within six months of the date of such approval.
evidence: Application for fresh registration filed with SEBI.
verbatim_text: i. The prior approval granted by SEBI shall be valid for a period of six months from the date of such approval within which the applicant shall file application for fresh registration pursuant to change in control.

title: File application with SEBI before NCLT application
summary: Investment Advisers must file an application with SEBI prior to filing the application with NCLT.
trigger: Upon scheme of arrangement involving NCLT sanction
required_action: File an application with SEBI before applying for NCLT approval.
evidence: Application filed with SEBI.
verbatim_text: i. The application seeking approval for the proposed change in control of the IA shall be filed with SEBI prior to filing the application with NCLT.

title: Obtain in-principle approval from SEBI
summary: Investment Advisers must obtain an in-principle approval from SEBI before proceeding with NCLT application.
trigger: Upon filing the application with SEBI for change in control involving scheme of arrangement requiring NCLT sanction
required_action: Obtain an in-principle approval from SEBI before proceeding to file the application with NCLT.
evidence: In-principle approval granted by SEBI.
verbatim_text: ii. Upon being satisfied with compliance of the applicable regulatory requirements, an in-principle approval will be granted by SEBI;

title: Submit NCLT order and related documents to SEBI within 15 days
summary: Investment Advisers must submit the relevant documents to SEBI within 15 days of receiving an NCLT order.
trigger: Upon receipt of NCLT order approving the scheme
required_action: Submit all required documents to SEBI within 15 days of receiving the NCLT order.
evidence: Submission of relevant documents to SEBI.
verbatim_text: iv. Within 15 days from the date of order of NCLT, the IA shall submit an online application in terms of clause 9.2 along with the following documents to SEBI for final approval:

title: Compliance with Advertisement Code
summary: Ensure all forms of communication that may influence investment decisions include the required disclosures.
trigger: Issuance of any form of advertisement or communication by IA.
required_action: Include all required disclosures in advertisements and communications.
evidence: Records of advertisements and communications, including the required disclosures.
source_circular: SEBI/HO/MIRSD/ MIRSD-PoD-2/P/CIR/2023/51 dated April 05, 2023 and SEBI/HO/MIRSD/ MIRSD-PoD-2/P/CIR/2023/52 dated April 06, 2023
verbatim_text: a. Forms of communication: i. Advertisement shall include all forms of communications, issued by or on behalf of IA, that may influence investment decisions of any investor or prospective investor. ii. The forms of communications, to which the advertisement code shall be applicable, shall include pamphlets, circulars, brochures, notices, research reports or any other literature, document, information or material published, or designed for use in any publication or displays (such as newspaper, magazine, sign boards/hoardings at any location), in any electronic, wired or wireless communication (such as electronic mail, text messaging, messaging platforms, social media platforms, radio, telephone, or in any other form over the internet) or over any other audio-visual form of communication (such as television, tape recording, video tape recordings, motion pictures) or in any other manner whatsoever.

title: Disclosure Requirements in Advertisements
summary: Include specific disclosures such as IA's name, address, registration number, and standard warning.
trigger: Issuance of any form of advertisement or communication by IA.
required_action: Ensure advertisements contain the required disclosures.
evidence: Records of advertisements and communications, including the required disclosures.
source_circular: SEBI/HO/MIRSD/ MIRSD-PoD-2/P/CIR/2023/51 dated April 05, 2023 and SEBI/HO/MIRSD/ MIRSD-PoD-2/P/CIR/2023/52 dated April 06, 2023
verbatim_text: b. Information/disclosures in the advertisement: The information/disclosures that the advertisement shall contain, include the following- i. Name of the IA/RA as registered with SEBI, registered office address, SEBI Registration No., logo/brand name/trade name of IA, and CIN of the IA, if applicable. ii. Information which is accurate, true and complete in unambiguous and concise language. iii. Standard warning in legible fonts (minimum 10 font size) which states “Investment in securities market are subject to market risks. Read all the related documents carefully before investing”. No addition or deletion of words shall be made to/from the standard warning. iv. In audio-visual media based advertisements, the standard warning in visual media based advertisement and accompanying voice over reiteration shall be audible in a clear and understandable manner. For example, in standard warning both the visual and the voice over reiteration containing 20 words running for at least 10 seconds may be considered as clear and understandable. v. Whenever the advertisement is being issued in a language other than English, it will be ensured that the standard warning is accurately translated in the language of the advertisement. vi. In case the mode of advertisement is SMS/Message/Pop-up, social media etc. and the details such as full name, logo/brand name, full registered office address, SEBI registration number, membership number of a SEBI recognized supervisory body and standard disclaimer are not mentioned, then official website hyperlink should be provided in such SMS/Message/Pop-up, etc. and the website must contain all such details.

title: Include Disclaimer in Advertisement
summary: Investment Advisers must include a disclaimer stating that the securities quoted are for illustration only and not recommendatory.
trigger: When displaying specific securities in advertisements as examples
required_action: Include the disclaimer 'The securities quoted are for illustration only and are not recommendatory.'
evidence: Website content or advertisement copy containing the disclaimer.
source_clause: vii. In case any specific security/ securities are displayed in the advertisement as examples, disclaimer that 'The securities quoted are for illustration only and are not recommendatory' should be mentioned.
verbatim_text: vii. In case any specific security/ securities are displayed in the advertisement as examples, disclaimer that 'The securities quoted are for illustration only and are not recommendatory' should be mentioned.

title: Include Client Disclaimer
summary: Investment Advisers must include a disclaimer stating that SEBI registration, membership of BASL, and NISM certification do not guarantee performance or provide any assurance of returns to investors.
trigger: When advertising services
required_action: Include the disclaimer 'Registration granted by SEBI, membership of BASL and certification from NISM in no way guarantee performance of the IA or provide any assurance of returns to investors.'
evidence: Website content or advertisement copy containing the disclaimer.
source_clause: viii. Advertisements and communications/correspondences with clients shall include the disclaimer that 'Registration granted by SEBI, membership of BASL and certification from NISM in no way guarantee performance of the IA or provide any assurance of returns to investors.'
verbatim_text: viii. Advertisements and communications/correspondences with clients shall include the disclaimer that 'Registration granted by SEBI, membership of BASL and certification from NISM in no way guarantee performance of the IA or provide any assurance of returns to investors.'

title: Prohibit Certain Content in Advertisements
summary: Investment Advisers must not include prohibited content, false statements, misleading information, testimonials, or any other content that may mislead investors.
trigger: When creating advertisements
required_action: Ensure advertisements do not contain prohibited content, false statements, misleading information, testimonials, or any other content that may mislead investors.
evidence: Review of advertisement materials and compliance with the listed prohibitions.
source_clause:
c. Prohibitions in the advertisement: The advertisement shall not contain:
(i) Anything which is prohibited for publication under the law.
(ii) Statements which are false, misleading, biased or deceptive, based on assumptions or projections.
(iii) Any misleading or deceptive testimonials.
(iv) Statements which, directly or by implication or by omission, may mislead the investor.
(v) Any statement likely to be misunderstood or likely to disguise the significance of the same or any other statement contained in the advertisement.
(vi) Any statement designed to exploit the lack of experience or knowledge of the investors.
(vii) Any statement that is exaggerated or is inconsistent with or unrelated to the nature and risk and return profile of the product.
(viii) Extensive use of technical or legal terminology or complex language and the inclusion of excessive details which may distract the investors.
(ix) Reference to any report, analysis, or service as free, unless it actually is free and without condition or obligation.
(x) Any promise or guarantee of assured or risk free return to the investors.
The advertisement shall not imply any assured returns or minimum returns or target return or percentage accuracy or service provision till achievement of target returns or any other nomenclature that gives the impression to the client that the investment advice is risk-free and/or not susceptible to market risks and/or that it can generate returns with any level of assurance.
(xi) Any statement which directly or indirectly discredits other advertisements or intermediaries or makes unfair comparisons or ascribes any qualitative advantage over other intermediaries directly or indirectly.

title: Obtain Prior Approval for Advertisements
summary: Investment Advisers must obtain prior approval from SEBI recognized supervisory body (BSE Administration & Supervision Ltd. (BASL)) before issuing advertisements.
trigger: Before issuing any advertisement
required_action: Obtain prior approval from SEBI recognized supervisory body (BSE Administration & Supervision Ltd. (BASL)).
evidence: Approval letter or document from BASL.
source_clause:
d. Other compliances/requirements:
i. Prior approval for the advertisement/material shall be obtained from SEBI recognized supervisory body (BSE Administration & Supervision Ltd. (BASL)) before issue.

trigger: During suspension period
required_action: Do not issue any advertisements during the suspension period.
evidence: Notification of suspension from SEBI or BASL and cessation of advertisement activities.

ii. In the event of suspension of any IA by SEBI and/or by SEBI recognized supervisory body, the IA so suspended shall not issue any advertisement either

title: Display of Additional Information in Correspondence with Clients
summary: Investment Advisers (IAs) must prominently display additional information such as the name, telephone number, and e-mail address of the compliance officer and grievance officer or cell in all client communications.
trigger: Issuing an advertisement or other communication
required_action: Display the required information prominently in all client communications.
evidence: Screenshots of displayed information and records of communications.
verbatim_text: The information such as name of the IA as registered with SEBI, its logo, its registration number, its complete address with telephone numbers, the name of the compliance officer, his telephone number and e-mail address, the name, telephone number and e-mail address of the grievance officer or the grievance redressal cell shall be displayed prominently in statements or reports or any other form of correspondence with the client.

title: Display of Disclaimer on All Communication Channels
summary: Investment Advisers (IAs) must display a disclaimer stating that SEBI registration, membership in BASL, and NISM certification do not guarantee performance or provide any assurance of returns to investors.
trigger: Issuing an advertisement or other communication
required_action: Display the disclaimer prominently on all relevant channels.
evidence: Screenshots of displayed information and records of communications.
verbatim_text: Disclaimer that “Registration granted by SEBI, membership of BASL and certification from NISM in no way guarantee performance of the IA or provide any assurance of returns to investors” shall be mentioned on portal/web site, if any, notice board, display boards, advertisements, publications, know your client forms, client agreements, statements or reports or any other form of correspondence with the client.

title: Use of Stock Exchange Infrastructure for Mutual Fund Transactions
summary: Investment Advisers (IAs) are allowed to use stock exchange infrastructure to purchase and redeem mutual fund units directly from Mutual Fund/Asset Management Companies on behalf of their clients.
trigger: Engaging in mutual fund transactions
required_action: Use the recognized stock exchanges' infrastructure for such transactions.
evidence: Transaction records and confirmations.
verbatim_text: Registered IAs are allowed to use infrastructure of the recognized stock exchanges to purchase and redeem mutual fund units directly from Mutual Fund/Asset Management Companies on behalf of their clients, including direct plans.

title: Prohibition on Unauthenticated News Circulation
summary: Investment Advisers (IAs) must put in place proper internal code of conduct and controls to prevent the circulation of unauthenticated news.
trigger: Circulating unauthenticated news
required_action: Implement a proper internal code of conduct and controls.
evidence: Documentation of implemented policies and procedures.
verbatim_text: Proper internal code of conduct and controls should be put in place.

title: Implement a proper internal code of conduct and controls
summary: Investment Advisers (IAs) must establish an appropriate internal code of conduct and control mechanisms.
trigger: At the inception or as part of regular compliance reviews
required_action: Put in place a proper internal code of conduct and controls
evidence: Documentation of the established code of conduct and control mechanisms
verbatim_text: Proper internal code of conduct and controls should be put in place.

title: Prevent employees from encouraging or circulating unverified information
summary: IAs must ensure that their employees do not spread unverified information.
trigger: At the inception and ongoing basis
required_action: Prohibit employees from spreading unverified information
evidence: Internal policies and procedures documentation
verbatim_text: Employees/temporary staff/voluntary workers etc. employed/working in the Offices of market intermediaries do not encourage or circulate rumours or unverified information obtained from client, industry, any trade or any other sources without verification.

title: Control access to blogs/chat forums/messenger sites
summary: IAs must manage their employees' access to online platforms.
trigger: At the inception and ongoing basis
required_action: Restrict or monitor access to such platforms
evidence: Access logs and monitoring records
verbatim_text: Access to Blogs/ Chat forums/Messenger sites etc. should either be restricted under supervision or access should not be allowed.

title: Maintain logs for usage of blogs/chat forums/messenger sites
summary: IAs must keep records of their employees' use of online platforms.
trigger: At the inception and ongoing basis
required_action: Maintain logs as per IA Regulations
evidence: Log maintenance records
verbatim_text: Logs for any usage of such Blogs/Chat forums/Messenger sites (called by any nomenclature) shall be treated as records and the same should be maintained as specified by the IA Regulations.

title: Forward market-related news only after approval
summary: IAs must ensure that their employees forward market-related information only after it has been reviewed.
trigger: Upon receipt of any market-related news
required_action: Forward the news only after approval by Compliance Officer
evidence: Approval logs and forwarding records
verbatim_text: Employees should be directed that any market related news received by them either in their official mail/personal mail/blog or in any other manner, should be forwarded only after the same has been seen and approved by the IA’s Compliance Officer. If an employee fails to do so, he/she shall be deemed to have violated the various provisions contained in SEBI Act/Rules/Regulations etc. and shall be liable for action. The Compliance Officer shall also be held liable for breach of duty in this regard.

title: Adhere to principles for outsourcing activities
summary: IAs must follow the principles outlined for outsourcing their activities.
trigger: When considering or engaging in outsourcing activities
required_action: Comply with the principles of outsourcing as per Annexure G
evidence: Documentation of compliance with the principles for outsourcing
verbatim_text: The risks associated with outsourcing may be operational risk, reputational risk, legal risk, country risk, strategic risk, exit-strategy risk, counter party risk, concentration and systemic risk. The principles for outsourcing are given in Annexure G.

title: Prohibit outsourcing of core business activities and compliance functions
summary: IAs must not outsource their core business or compliance functions.
trigger: When considering or engaging in outsourcing activities
required_action: Do not outsource core business activities and compliance functions
evidence: Documentation of the decision to retain control over core activities and compliance functions
verbatim_text: The intermediaries desirous of outsourcing their activities shall not, however, outsource their core business activities and compliance functions. An example of core business activity may be – execution of orders and monitoring of trading activities of clients in case of stock brokers.

title: Comply with KYC requirements
summary: IAs must comply with the provisions related to Know Your Client (KYC) as per SEBI regulations.
trigger: At all times and during client onboarding
required_action: Comply with KYC requirements from time to time
evidence: Documentation of compliance with KYC provisions
verbatim_text: Regarding Know Your Client (KYC) requirements, the intermediaries shall comply with the provisions of SEBI {KYC (Know Your Client) Registration Agency} Regulations, 2011 and Guidelines issued thereunder from time to time.

title: Reporting Suspicious Transactions to FIU
summary: Investment Advisers (IAs) must report suspicious transactions or reports to the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) or any other competent authority.
trigger: Carrying out activities with third parties that may involve suspicious transactions
required_action: Reporting such transactions/reports to FIU or relevant authority
evidence: Records of reports submitted to FIU
source_clause: 13.6. Other Obligations: Reporting to Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU)
verbatim_text: The intermediaries shall be responsible for reporting of any suspicious transactions / reports to FIU or any other competent authority in respect of activities carried out by the third parties.

title: Participation in Regulatory Sandbox
summary: Investment Advisers (IAs) can participate in a regulatory sandbox to experiment with FinTech solutions.
trigger: Wishing to test new financial technology solutions in a live environment
required_action: Participate in the sandbox and follow its guidelines
evidence: Participation agreement or documentation
source_clause: 14.2. The guidelines pertaining to the functioning of the Regulatory Sandbox are available at the link below:
verbatim_text: The guidelines pertaining to the functioning of the Regulatory Sandbox are available at the link below: https://www.sebi.gov.in/legal/circulars/jun-2021/revised-framework-for-regulatory-sandbox_50521.html and https://www.sebi.gov.in/legal/circulars/nov-2021/framework-for-regulatory-sandbox_53982.html

title: Avoiding or Managing Conflict of Interest
summary: Investment Advisers (IAs) must avoid or manage conflicts of interest and ensure fair treatment of clients.
trigger: Engaging in activities that may create a conflict of interest
required_action: Developing policies, procedures, and codes to identify and deal with conflicts of interest; maintaining high standards of integrity; ensuring fair treatment of clients
evidence: Policies, procedures, internal code of conduct, communication records
source_clause: 15.4. Intermediaries and their associated persons shall, i. lay down, with active involvement of senior management, policies and internal procedures to identify and avoid or to deal or manage actual or potential conflict of interest, develop an internal code of conduct governing operations and formulate standards of appropriate conduct in the performance of their activities, and ensure to communicate such policies, procedures and code to all concerned; ii. at all times maintain high standards of integrity in the conduct of their business; iii. ensure fair treatment of their clients and not discriminate amongst them;
verbatim_text: Intermediaries and their associated persons shall, i. lay down, with active involvement of senior management, policies and internal procedures to identify and avoid or to deal or manage actual or potential conflict of interest, develop an internal code of conduct governing operations and formulate standards of appropriate conduct in the performance of their activities, and ensure to communicate such policies, procedures and code to all concerned; ii. at all times maintain high standards of integrity in the conduct of their business; iii. ensure fair treatment of their clients and not discriminate amongst them;

title: Maintain High Standards of Integrity
summary: Investment Advisers (IAs) must maintain high standards of integrity in their business conduct.
trigger: At all times during the IA's operations
required_action: Adhere to high standards of integrity
evidence: Internal policies and procedures, compliance records
verbatim_text: iii. ensure fair treatment of their clients and not discriminate amongst them;

title: Fair Treatment of Clients
summary: IAs must ensure fair treatment of all clients without discrimination.
trigger: At all times during the IA's operations and when dealing with clients
required_action: Treat all clients fairly and equally
evidence: Client service records, internal policies
verbatim_text: iii. ensure fair treatment of their clients and not discriminate amongst them;

title: Disclosure of Conflicts of Interest
summary: IAs must disclose any potential conflicts of interest that could impair the provision of fair, objective, and unbiased services.
trigger: When providing investment advice or handling client mandates
required_action: Make appropriate disclosures to clients about possible sources or areas of conflict of interest
evidence: Disclosure documents, internal records
verbatim_text: v. make appropriate disclosure to the clients of possible source or potential areas of conflict of interest which would impair their ability to render fair, objective and unbiased services;

title: Management of Conflicts of Interest
summary: IAs must implement measures to reduce opportunities for conflicts through information barriers or other prescriptive methods.
trigger: When handling client mandates or securities transactions
required_action: Implement systems and procedures to manage conflicts of interest
evidence: Internal policies, compliance records
verbatim_text: vi. endeavor to reduce opportunities for conflict through prescriptive measures such as through information barriers to block or hinder the flow of information from one department/unit to another, etc.;

title: Restrictions on Transactions in Securities
summary: IAs must place appropriate restrictions on transactions involving securities while handling a mandate of an issuer or client.
trigger: When handling securities transactions for clients or issuers
required_action: Place appropriate restrictions to avoid conflicts
evidence: Transaction records, internal policies
verbatim_text: vii. place appropriate restrictions on transactions in securities while handling a mandate of issuer or client in respect of such security so as to avoid any conflict;

title: Prohibition on Using Material Non-Public Information
summary: IAs must not use material non-public information for their own benefit or that of others.
trigger: When in possession of material non-public information
required_action: Not deal in securities while possessing such information and not communicate it to others
evidence: Internal policies, compliance records
verbatim_text: viii. not deal in securities while in possession of material non published information; ix. not to communicate the material non published information while dealing in securities on behalf of others;

title: Prevent Market Manipulation
summary: IAs must not contribute to market manipulation or influence prices through improper means.
trigger: At all times during the IA's operations and when dealing in securities
required_action: Avoid actions that could manipulate markets or influence security prices
evidence: Internal policies, compliance records
verbatim_text: x. not in any way contribute to manipulate the demand for or supply of securities in the market or to influence prices of securities;

title: Risk Profiling and Incentive Structure
summary: IAs must not have an incentive structure that encourages the sale of products unsuitable for clients based on their risk profile.
trigger: When designing or implementing sales incentives
required_action: Ensure that the incentive structure does not encourage the sale of inappropriate products
evidence: Incentive plan documentation, compliance records
verbatim_text: xi. not have an incentive structure that encourages sale of products not suitable the risk profile of their clients;

title: Protection of Client Information
summary: IAs must not share client information obtained through dealings for personal gain.
trigger: When handling client information and transactions
required_action: Not use or share client information for personal benefit
evidence: Internal policies, compliance records
verbatim_text: xii. not share information received from clients or pertaining to them, obtained as a result of their dealings, for their personal interest;

title: Board Review of Compliance
summary: Boards of intermediaries must implement systems and provide guidance to manage conflicts of interest.
trigger: At all times during the IA's operations
required_action: Implement systems for conflict management and review compliance periodically
evidence: Board meeting minutes, internal policies
verbatim_text: The Boards of intermediaries shall put in place systems for implementation of the aforementioned guidelines and provide necessary guidance enabling identification, elimination or management of conflict of interest situations. The Boards shall review the compliance of the above guidelines periodically.

title: Guidelines on Data Access and Usage
summary: IAs must follow specific guidelines for accessing and using data from Indian securities markets.
trigger: When accessing or using market data
required_action: Follow the guidelines for free and chargeable data access and usage
evidence: Data access logs, internal policies
verbatim_text: Further, apart from the data made available free of cost, data which is chargeable should be appropriately identified as such in public domain.

required_action: Refer to specified circulars for KYC norms.
evidence: Documentation showing adherence to the KYC norms as per the referenced circulars.
verbatim_text: IAs are advised to refer to the following master circular no. SEBI/HO/MIRSD/SECFATF/P/CIR/2023/169 dated October 12, 2023 on ‘Know Your Client (KYC) norms for securities market’ available on SEBI website at https://www.sebi.gov.in/legal/master-circulars/oct-2023/master-circular-on-know-your-client-kyc-norms-for-the-securities-market_77945.html

title: Compliance with Accreditation Requirements
summary: Investment Advisers (IAs) must comply with the requirements for grant of accreditation to investors.
trigger: Being an Investment Adviser
required_action: Refer to specified circulars for accreditation requirements.
evidence: Documentation showing adherence to the accreditation requirements as per the referenced circulars.
verbatim_text: IAs are advised to refer to the following circulars with respect to accreditation to investors: i. Circular No. SEBI/HO/IMD/IMD-I/DF9/P/CIR/2021/620 dated August 26, 2021 on ‘Modalities for implementation of the framework for Accredited Investors available at: https://www.sebi.gov.in/legal/circulars/aug-2021/circular-on-modalities-for-implementation-of-the-framework-for-accredited-investors_52116.html ii. Circular No. SEBI/HO/AFD/PoD1/CIR/2023/189 dated December 18, 2023 on ‘Simplification of requirements for grant of accreditation to investors” available at: https://www.sebi.gov.in/legal/circulars/dec-2023/simplification-of-requirements-for-grant-of-accreditation-to-investors_79990.html

title: Periodic Reporting for Investment Advisers
summary: Investment Advisers (IAs) must submit periodic reports as per the specified format.
trigger: Being an Investment Adviser
required_action: Submit periodic reports in the prescribed format.

verbatim_text: Don’t fall for the promise of indicative or exorbitant or assured returns by the Investment Advisers. Don’t let greed overcome rational investment decisions.

verbatim_text: (v) No order of conviction has been passed against us by a court for any offence involving moral turpitude.

verbatim_text: (vi) No winding up proceedings have been initiated or an order for winding up has been passed against us.

verbatim_text: (vii) We have not been declared insolvent.

verbatim_text: (viii) We have not been found to be of unsound mind by a court of competent jurisdiction and no such finding is in force.

title: Comprehensive Policy for Outsourcing Activities
summary: Investment Advisers must have a comprehensive policy in place to guide the assessment of whether and how activities can be appropriately outsourced.
trigger: Outsourcing activities are being considered
required_action: Develop and implement an outsourcing policy
evidence: Documentation of the outsourcing policy
verbatim_text: 1. An intermediary seeking to outsource activities shall have in place a comprehensive policy to guide the assessment of whether and how those activities can be appropriately outsourced.

title: Board Responsibility for Outsourcing Policy
summary: Investment Advisers must ensure that the Board is responsible for the outsourcing policy and related overall responsibility for activities undertaken under that policy.
trigger: Outsourcing activities are being considered
required_action: Ensure the Board's responsibility for the outsourcing policy
evidence: Documentation of the Board's role in the outsourcing policy
verbatim_text: 1. An intermediary seeking to outsource activities shall have in place a comprehensive policy to guide the assessment of whether and how those activities can be appropriately outsourced. The Board / partners (as the case may be) {hereinafter referred to as the “the Board”} of the intermediary shall have the responsibility for the outsourcing policy and related overall responsibility for activities undertaken under that policy.

title: Policy Covers Activities, Authorities, and Third Party Selection
summary: Investment Advisers must ensure their outsourcing policy covers the activities or nature of activities that can be outsourced, the authorities who can approve such outsourcing, and the selection of third parties to whom it can be outsourced.
trigger: Outsourcing activities are being considered
required_action: Ensure the policy covers all required aspects
evidence: Documentation of the outsourcing policy
verbatim_text: 1.1. The policy shall cover activities or the nature of activities that can be outsourced, the authorities who can approve outsourcing of such activities, and the selection of third party to whom it can be outsourced.

title: Regularly review outsourcing policy
summary: Periodically assess the outsourcing policy to ensure it remains relevant.
trigger: On a regular basis as per the established schedule
required_action: Conduct periodic reviews of the outsourcing policy.
evidence: Review reports and minutes of meetings
verbatim_text: The Board shall mandate a regular review of outsourcing policy for such activities in the wake of changing business environment. It shall also have overall responsibility for ensuring that all ongoing outsourcing decisions taken by the intermediary and the activities undertaken by the third-party, are in keeping with its outsourcing policy.

title: Assess outsourcing risk
summary: Evaluate risks associated with outsourced activities.
trigger: Before engaging in any outsourcing activity
required_action: Conduct a comprehensive assessment of the risks involved in outsourcing activities.
evidence: Risk assessment report
verbatim_text: An intermediary shall make an assessment of outsourcing risk which depends on several factors, including the scope and materiality of the outsourced activity, etc.

title: Consider specific factors in risk assessment
summary: Identify key factors to consider when assessing outsourcing risks.
trigger: During the risk assessment process
required_action: Evaluate various factors such as impact on financial performance, ability to cope with non-performance, regulatory status of third party, and conflict of interest measures.
evidence: Risk assessment report detailing considered factors

title: Maintain arm's length distance with related parties
summary: Ensure that outsourcing to a group entity or associate maintains an arm's length relationship.
trigger: When considering outsourcing to a related party
required_action: Implement systems to maintain an arm's length distance between the intermediary and the third party in terms of infrastructure, manpower, decision-making, record keeping, etc.
evidence: Documentation showing implementation of arm's length practices
verbatim_text: While there shall not be any prohibition on a group entity / associate of the intermediary to act as the third party, systems shall be put in place to have an arm’s length distance between the intermediary and the third party in terms of infrastructure, manpower, decision-making, record keeping, etc. for avoidance of potential conflict of interests. Necessary disclosures in this regard shall be made as part of the contractual agreement. It shall be kept in mind that the risk management practices expected to be adopted by an intermediary while outsourcing to a related party or an associate would be identical to those followed while outsourcing to an unrelated party.

title: Centralize record keeping for outsourced activities
summary: Maintain central records of all outsourced activities.
trigger: Upon engaging in any outsourcing activity
required_action: Preserve records centrally so that they are readily accessible for review by the Board or senior management.
evidence: Centralized record-keeping system and documentation
verbatim_text: The records relating to all activities outsourced shall be preserved centrally so that the same is readily accessible for review by the Board of the intermediary and / or its senior management, as and when needed. Such records shall be regularly updated and may also form part of the corporate governance review by the management of the intermediary.

title: Maintain Regularly Updated Records
summary: Regularly update and maintain records that may form part of the corporate governance review by management.
trigger: Outsourcing activities
required_action: Maintain regularly updated records.
evidence: Records maintained as per the circular.
verbatim_text: Such records shall be regularly updated and may also form part of the corporate governance review by the management of the intermediary.

title: Regular Reviews by Auditors
summary: Conduct regular reviews by internal or external auditors on outsourcing policies, risk management system, and regulatory requirements.
trigger: Board's discretion
required_action: Conduct regular reviews by internal or external auditors.
evidence: Audit reports and review records.
verbatim_text: Regular reviews by internal or external auditors of the outsourcing policies, risk management system and requirements of the regulator shall be mandated by the Board wherever felt necessary.

title: Ensure Outsourcing Does Not Diminish Obligations to Customers and Regulators
summary: Ensure outsourcing arrangements do not diminish the ability to fulfill obligations to customers and regulators.
trigger: Outsourcing activities
required_action: Ensure that outsourcing does not diminish the ability to fulfill obligations.
evidence: Documentation of due diligence, risk assessments, and compliance checks.
verbatim_text: The intermediary shall ensure that outsourcing arrangements neither diminish its ability to fulfill its obligations to customers and regulators, nor impede effective supervision by the regulators.

title: Full Liability for Outsourced Activities
summary: Be fully liable and accountable for activities outsourced to third parties as if they were provided in-house.
trigger: Outsourcing arrangements
required_action: Be fully liable and accountable for the activities outsourced.
evidence: Documentation of due diligence, risk assessments, and compliance checks.
verbatim_text: The intermediary shall be fully liable and accountable for the activities that are being outsourced to the same extent as if the service were provided in-house.

title: Protect Investor Rights
summary: Ensure outsourcing arrangements do not affect investors' rights and be liable for any loss incurred by them.
trigger: Outsourcing activities
required_action: Ensure that outsourcing does not affect investor rights and be liable for losses.
evidence: Documentation of due diligence, risk assessments, and compliance checks.
verbatim_text: Outsourcing arrangements shall not affect the rights of an investor or client against the intermediary in any manner. The intermediary shall be liable to the investors for the loss incurred by them due to the failure of the third party and also be responsible for redressal of the grievances received from investors arising out of activities rendered by the third party.

title: Access to Outsourced Facilities/Premises/Data
summary: Intermediary and SEBI/SRO or authorized persons have the right to access facilities, premises, and data involved in outsourced activities.
trigger: Outsourcing arrangements
required_action: Ensure that intermediaries and SEBI/SRO or authorized persons can access relevant facilities, premises, and data.
evidence: Documentation of due diligence, risk assessments, and compliance checks.
verbatim_text: The facilities / premises / data that are involved in carrying out the outsourced activity by the service provider shall be deemed to be those of the registered intermediary. The intermediary itself and Regulator or the persons authorized by it shall have the right to access the same at any point of time.

title: Regulatory Supervision Not Impaired
summary: Ensure outsourcing arrangements do not impair SEBI/SRO's regulatory responsibilities.
trigger: Outsourcing activities
required_action: Ensure that outsourcing does not impair the ability of SEBI/SRO or auditors to exercise their regulatory responsibilities.
evidence: Documentation of due diligence, risk assessments, and compliance checks.
verbatim_text: Outsourcing arrangements shall not impair the ability of SEBI/SRO or auditors to exercise its regulatory responsibilities such as supervision/inspection of the intermediary.

title: Due Diligence in Selecting Third Parties
summary: Conduct appropriate due diligence in selecting third parties and monitoring their performance.
trigger: Outsourcing arrangements
required_action: Conduct appropriate due diligence in selecting third parties and monitor their performance.
evidence: Documentation of due diligence, risk assessments, and compliance checks.
verbatim_text: The intermediary shall conduct appropriate due diligence in selecting the third party and in monitoring of its performance.

title: Exercise Due Care in Selecting Third Parties
summary: Exercise due care, skill, and diligence in selecting third parties to ensure their ability and capacity.
trigger: Outsourcing arrangements
required_action: Exercise due care, skill, and diligence in the selection of third parties.
evidence: Documentation of due diligence, risk assessments, and compliance checks.
verbatim_text: It is important that the intermediary exercises due care, skill, and diligence in the selection of the third party to ensure that the third party has the ability and capacity to undertake the provision of the service effectively.

title: Due Diligence Assessment Criteria
summary: Assess third parties based on their resources, compatibility with requirements, market feedback, concentration risk, and foreign environment.
trigger: Outsourcing arrangements
required_action: Conduct due diligence assessment of third parties using specified criteria.
evidence: Documentation of due diligence, risk assessments, and compliance checks.
verbatim_text: The due diligence undertaken by an intermediary shall include assessment of: (a) third party’s resources and capabilities, including financial soundness, to perform the outsourcing work within the timelines fixed; (b) compatibility of the practices and systems of the third party with the intermediary's requirements and objectives; (c) market feedback of the prospective third party's business reputation and track record of their services rendered in the past; (d) level of concentration of the outsourced arrangements with a single third party; and (e) the environment of the foreign country where the third party is located.

title: Contract for Outsourcing Arrangements
summary: Investment Advisers must have a written contract with third parties for outsourcing arrangements.
trigger: Outsourcing of activities to third parties
required_action: Enter into a clearly defined and legally binding written contract.
evidence: Copies of the contracts with third parties.
verbatim_text: Outsourcing arrangements shall be governed by a clearly defined and legally binding written contract between the intermediary and each of the third parties, the nature and detail of which shall be appropriate to the materiality of the outsourced activity in relation to the ongoing business of the intermediary.

title: Clear Definition of Outsourced Activities
summary: Investment Advisers must clearly define what activities are being outsourced and include appropriate service and performance levels.
trigger: Outsourcing of activities to third parties
required_action: Clearly define the activities, including appropriate service and performance levels in the contract.
evidence: Copies of the contracts with clear definitions of outsourced activities.
verbatim_text: clearly defines what activities are going to be outsourced, including appropriate service and performance levels;

title: Mutual Rights, Obligations, and Responsibilities in Contracts
summary: Investment Advisers must include mutual rights, obligations, and responsibilities of the intermediary and third party in contracts.
trigger: Outsourcing of activities to third parties
required_action: Include mutual rights, obligations, and responsibilities in the contract.
evidence: Copies of the contracts with mutual rights, obligations, and responsibilities.
verbatim_text: provides for mutual rights, obligations and responsibilities of the intermediary and the third party, including indemnity by the parties;

title: Liability of Third Party for Unsatisfactory Performance
summary: Investment Advisers must ensure that the contract includes provisions for liability of third party in case of unsatisfactory performance.
trigger: Outsourcing of activities to third parties
required_action: Include provisions for liability of the third party in the contract.
evidence: Copies of the contracts with liability provisions.
verbatim_text: provides for the liability of the third party to the intermediary for unsatisfactory performance/other breach of the contract

title: Continuous Monitoring and Assessment by Intermediary
summary: Investment Advisers must continuously monitor and assess third parties to ensure compliance with legal and regulatory obligations.
trigger: Outsourcing of activities to third parties
required_action: Continuously monitor and assess the third party for compliance with legal and regulatory obligations.
evidence: Monitoring reports or records.
verbatim_text: provides for the continuous monitoring and assessment by the intermediary of the third party so that any necessary corrective measures can be taken up immediately, i.e., the contract shall enable the intermediary to retain an appropriate level of control over the outsourcing and the right to intervene with appropriate measures to meet legal and regulatory obligations;

title: Conditions for Sub-Contracting by Third Party
summary: Investment Advisers must ensure that contracts include conditions for sub-contracting by third parties.
trigger: Outsourcing of activities to third parties
required_action: Include conditions for sub-contracting by the third party in the contract.
evidence: Copies of the contracts with sub-contracting provisions.
verbatim_text: includes, where necessary, conditions of sub-contracting by the third-party, i.e. the contract shall enable intermediary to maintain a similar control over the risks when a third party outsources to further third parties as in the original direct outsourcing;

title: Confidentiality Clauses in Contracts
summary: Investment Advisers must include unambiguous confidentiality clauses in contracts.
trigger: Outsourcing of activities to third parties
required_action: Include unambiguous confidentiality clauses in the contract.
evidence: Copies of the contracts with confidentiality clauses.
verbatim_text: has unambiguous confidentiality clauses to ensure protection of proprietary and customer data during the tenure of the contract and also after the expiry of the contract;

title: IT Security and Contingency Plans in Contracts
summary: Investment Advisers must ensure that contracts include provisions for IT security, contingency plans, insurance cover, business continuity, and disaster recovery.
trigger: Outsourcing of activities to third parties
required_action: Include provisions for IT security, contingency plans, insurance cover, business continuity, and disaster recovery in the contract.
evidence: Copies of the contracts with IT security and contingency plan provisions.
verbatim_text: provides for the responsibilities of the third party with respect to the IT security and contingency plans, insurance cover, business continuity and disaster recovery plans, force majeure clause, etc;

title: Preservation of Documents and Data by Third Party
summary: Investment Advisers must ensure that contracts include provisions for the preservation of documents and data.
trigger: Outsourcing of activities to third parties
required_action: Include provisions for the preservation of documents and data in the contract.
evidence: Copies of the contracts with data preservation provisions.
verbatim_text: provides for preservation of the documents and data by third party;

title: Mechanisms to Resolve Disputes in Contracts
summary: Investment Advisers must ensure that contracts include mechanisms to resolve disputes arising from the implementation of the outsourcing contract.
trigger: Outsourcing of activities to third parties
required_action: Include mechanisms for dispute resolution in the contract.
evidence: Copies of the contracts with dispute resolution provisions.
verbatim_text: provides for the mechanisms to resolve disputes arising from implementation of the outsourcing contract;

title: Termination and Exit Strategies in Contracts
summary: Investment Advisers must ensure that contracts include provisions for termination, termination rights, transfer of information, and exit strategies.
trigger: Outsourcing of activities to third parties

verbatim_text: 6.3. To ensure business continuity, robust information technology security is a necessity. Intermediaries shall, therefore, seek to ensure that third party maintains appropriate IT security and robust disaster recovery capabilities.

title: Protect Confidential Information
summary: Ensure that confidential information is protected from intentional or inadvertent disclosure.
trigger: Outsourcing arrangements are in place.
required_action: Take appropriate steps to protect proprietary and confidential customer information, limit access to data on a 'need-to-know' basis, and ensure adequate checks and balances.
evidence: Confidentiality agreements, access logs, and records of regular reviews.
verbatim_text:
7. The intermediary shall take appropriate steps to require that third parties protect confidential information of both the intermediary and its customers from intentional or inadvertent disclosure to unauthorised persons.

7.1. An intermediary that engages in outsourcing is expected to take appropriate steps to protect its proprietary and confidential customer information and ensure that it is not misused or misappropriated.

7.2. The intermediary shall prevail upon the third party to ensure that the employees of the third party have limited access to the data handled and only on a ‘need to know’ basis and the third party shall have adequate checks and balances to ensure the same.

7.3. In cases where the third party is providing similar services to multiple entities, the intermediary shall ensure that adequate care is taken by the third party to build safeguards for data security and confidentiality.
